title: The US didn't need India's product. I had three weeks to prove it.
shortTitle: The US didn't need India's product. I had three weeks to prove it.
description: Filo matched students with live tutors in seconds and already had 2M+ users. The plan for the US was a lift-and-shift. I pushed for US-specific matching, proved the case in three weeks, and the US marketplace reached 120K users and $1.5M ARR in six months.
problem: Filo matched students with live tutors in seconds and already had 2M+ users. The plan for the US was a lift-and-shift. I pushed for US-specific matching, proved the case in three weeks, and the US marketplace reached 120K users and $1.5M ARR in six months.
decision: Build US-specific matching for collaborative learning instead of porting the India model.
scope: Founding US PM, owning the US launch while based in India: matching, the activation funnel, OCR intake, session continuity, low-bandwidth audio and video, student and tutor onboarding, quality thresholds, and fraud detection. Worked with engineering, data science, and a 200-person operations team.

sections.label: The Problem
sections.title: The easy path was already decided.

paragraphs.text: The playbook had worked at 2M+ users, so the plan for the US was reasonable on paper: take the matching model that worked in India and ship it.

sections.label: What I Found
sections.title: US students didn't want answers. They wanted to learn together.

paragraphs.text: Across 100+ user interviews, US students behaved fundamentally differently. They wanted a collaborative learning experience, not the model that worked in India.

sections.label: The Decision
sections.title: Fight for the harder path, and prove it fast.

paragraphs.text: I pushed for US-specific matching logic. I was given three weeks to prove the US needed it. The cost was personal: a lean team, lost sleep, and keeping momentum under pressure while the default plan was ready to go.
Matching had a 60-second target. We designed the whole request path around it.

sections.label: Outcomes
sections.title: 120K users and $1.5M ARR in six months.

paragraphs.text: Activation rose 35% and conversion reached 3%+. 98% of US requests were matched in under 45 seconds, against a 60-second target.

sections.label: What I Learned
sections.title: Local insight is a product decision, not a localization task.

paragraphs.text: Building US-specific matching wasn't the hardest part. The hardest part was earning the three weeks to prove it was needed.
